issues: Verification date 2026-08-19 is beyond reviewer knowledge cutoff; claimed install states (imsg present, memo/remindctl absent) cannot be independently confirmed
'remindctl' in steipete/tap is unverified — the widely documented Reminders CLI is 'rem' (reminders-cli); confirm this formula actually exists or substitute a known tool
memo and imsg both come from third-party Homebrew taps (antoniorodr/memo, steipete/tap) rather than homebrew-core; third-party taps go stale frequently — doc lacks upstream repo URLs for verification
Status header references 'All references/ docs verified present' but no upstream source links are provided to check tool deprecation
Excerpt truncated mid-iMessage-section ('Permission: Gr'), so permission instructions and remaining body cannot be fully assessed
AppleScript-based automation is aging but not deprecated; no mention of Shortcuts CLI ('shortcuts run') as a modern alternative — optional modernization, not an error

Model capability claims are aging: 'other models are often only reliable with indices' was more accurate in early 2024; newer models (GPT-4.1/CUA via Operator, Gemini 2.x) handle pixel coordinates far more reliably, so the blanket statement needs revision.

'Claude was trained on both' refers to an older training snapshot and ignores that Anthropic's official computer use tool (computer_20241022 / computer_20250124 schema versions) is coordinate-based with its own action set — the 'no Anthropic-native schema to learn' framing could mislead if the environment adds the official tool alongside this wrapper.

Tool parameters (capture, som/vision/ax modes, capture_after, element-index clicking) appear to be a custom wrapper with no version, changelog, or source link, so freshness cannot be independently verified — a link to the tool's repo/docs should be included.

No mention of macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording (TCC) permission requirements, which are a current prerequisite for AX-tree reading and background screenshot capture on recent macOS versions — a relevance gap.
No macOS version compatibility stated; AX role names and background-capture behavior (e.g., per-Space capture) have changed across macOS releases and should be pinned to tested versions.

No dead links or deprecated public APIs found in the excerpt — the core SOM + AX-index workflow itself remains a current pattern; the staleness is confined to comparative model claims and missing environment prerequisites.
Verification limited to first 2000 chars of body; full contents, links, and reference-file internals beyond the excerpt could not be checked
Claim that all 5 references/ files are 'verified present' and 'fleet domains current' is asserted by the header but not independently verifiable from the excerpt
Obsidian and cron are current, non-deprecated tooling; no dead links or deprecated patterns visible in provided content
Internal dates are consistent (loop-engineering update Jul 4, 2026 precedes review stamp Aug 23, 2026), suggesting active maintenance

Claude Code, Codex CLI (@openai/codex), and OpenCode are all actively maintained tools as of the review knowledge cutoff — no deprecated tools detected, but these agent CLIs iterate quickly and this review cannot verify post-cutoff status
hermes-agent and its delegate_task/cron tooling are not publicly documented tools — likely internal infrastructure; verify this related skill still exists in the library
Relative reference files (references/claude-code.md, references/codex.md, references/opencode.md) cannot be verified to exist from this excerpt
Codex CLI reference could be confused with the deprecated 2021-2023 Codex model; the @openai/codex package is the current Rust-based CLI, but a clarifying note would prevent ambiguity
No 'last reviewed' date or version anchors in the doc, making future freshness drift harder to detect

References 'cua-driver' as the tool driven under the hood, but the linked repo (github.com/trycua/cua) ships the 'cua' CLI / Python SDK — no 'cua-driver' binary or 'cua-driver skills install' command is known to exist; the tool name and install path (~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver) are unverifiable and possibly invented or renamed

Contains a roadmap-dependent claim ('Hermes autodetection is a planned cua-driver follow-up') plus a manual symlink workaround — exactly the kind of temporary instruction that rots quickly and should be re-verified against the current release

Claim that 'Claude was trained on both' element-index clicking and pixel coordinates is dubious: Anthropic's documented computer-use tool is coordinate/screenshot-based; index-based clicking is a wrapper convention (Set-of-Marks), not something Claude was specifically trained on
Naming collides confusingly with OpenAI's 'CUA' (computer-using agent / computer_use_preview in the Responses API, 2025) — doc should disambiguate trycua vs OpenAI CUA

Says 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' without acknowledging the now-standard Anthropic computer-use tool versions (computer_20241022, computer_20250124), which a maintainer may want to cross-reference

Strong claim that actions never steal cursor/keyboard focus is technically questionable for host-desktop driving (AX set-value vs synthesized events) and is not a guarantee the underlying driver makes

Cannot fully verify link liveness or current trycua API surface from static review; content appears roughly contemporary with 2024–2025 computer-use tooling but the driver-specific CLI, paths, and roadmap notes should be checked against the live repo before trusting them

References `delegate_task` as the subagent-spawning mechanism; this is not a current standard tool name in major agent frameworks (Claude Code uses `Task`), suggesting an internal, renamed, or deprecated API with no fallback named

Depends on `hermes kanban show` and `kanban_create(title=..., assignee=..., parents=[...])`, which appear to be internal/niche tooling with no public documentation or version pinning; existence and current schema (especially the `parents` kwarg) cannot be verified

Kanban integration is load-bearing in the 'Spawned neutral agent' section, so if the kanban tool's API has drifted, the preferred invocation path silently breaks; only the Standalone path is tool-agnostic
No URLs present in the provided excerpt, so dead links cannot be ruled out for the full body; no links to docs/specs for the referenced tools are given for verification
Minor: 'AGENTS' is used capitalized without defining the term (presumably AGENTS.md-convention agents), which is current but ambiguous to readers outside the assumed internal context

Core content is otherwise current: git merge/rebase/worktree conflict patterns, merge-queue arbiter framing, and neutral-third-party adjudication for parallel agent campaigns remain valid, non-deprecated practices
